item.title: [The Guardian — Photos of the Day] The week around the world in 20 pictures
item.source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day
item.description:
Kramatorsk, Ukraine — Oleksandr, a soldier, lifts his bride, Tetiana, a medic, on their wedding day. Getting married in Kramatorsk, Oleksandr says, is a necessary act of memory, because soon there may not be much more left to survive. ‘In this war, all this can just be vaporised, in a few months, in a few days,’ the groom explains immediately after the ceremony. ‘On the battlefield, many cities, towns, small villages where I was two, three years ago, they are now just ruins, just destroyed’. — Photograph: Julia Kochetova/The Guardian

Source: The Guardian — Photos of the Day

Kampar, Indonesia — Police in firefighting gear extinguish a peatland fire at Tambang in Kampar. Indonesia’s unique rainforests are home to peatland ecosystems, which should be naturally resilient to fire when water tables remain high. However, drainage networks built to clear land for pulp and oil palm plantations have robbed the soil of its natural capacity to retain water, experts say. — Photograph: WAHYUDI/AFP/Getty Images

Al-Mansouri, Lebanon — Smoke rises from the site of several Israeli airstrikes that targeted the area of al-Mansouri. The latest round of war has hardened existing divisions over Hezbollah. The group’s supporters accuse the government of humiliating Lebanon by negotiating directly with Israel and not responding to its attacks. Hezbollah’s opponents blame the group for provoking a war by launching rockets at Israel on 2 March, triggering Israel’s invasion and current occupation. — Photograph: Kawnat Haju/AFP/Getty Images

Bidur, Nepal — People react after the flood disaster at an army barracks in Bidur, where Nepal’s rescue efforts were being co-ordinated. The Red Cross has said at least 93,000 people may have been affected by Wednesday’s flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border, which have killed nearly 600 people, left another 1,900 missing, and triggered a huge rescue operation that is being hampered by fears of new flooding. — Photograph: Ahmer Khan/The Guardian

Nuwakot, Nepal — Residents look at the devastation left by flash flooding in Nuwakhot. The international community is scrambling to get aid into flood-stricken parts of Nepal and Tibet but search and rescue efforts – including for hundreds of tourists – have been complicated by the destruction of dozens of bridges and miles of roads in the mountainous region, which is popular with trekkers and pilgrims. — Photograph: Sanjit Pariyar/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Viacheslav Madiievskyi / Ukrinform / Future Publishing / Getty — People watch small songbirds fly out of a cage during a traditional release of rescued birds at Feldman Ecopark, in the Kharkiv region of Ukraine, on April 12, 2026. This year, more than 300 rescued birds (songbirds, pheasants, owls, swans, and partridges) were released into the wild. All of them underwent rehabilitation at the Dobryi Dim (Good Home) Feldman Ecopark Animal Rescue Center after injuries from Russian attacks, entanglement in anti-drone nets, or poachers.

item.title: [The Atlantic — Photography] Photos: Releasing Animals Back Into Their Habitats
item.source: The Atlantic — Photography
item.description:
Sean Gallup / Getty — Lutz Krenkel, a fisherman with the Regional Fishery Office of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, prepares to release a three-year-old Baltic sturgeon into the Oder River as his colleague Stefanie Felsing assists, on May 24, 2023, in Lebus, Germany. The sturgeon, along with 700 others that had been bred in captivity, was released into the Oder in an ongoing repopulation effort. The Baltic sturgeon was once common to the entire Baltic Sea region, though overfishing and waterway development led to its practical extinction by the 1950s.

Source: The Atlantic — Photography
